poles: Living wage / no one working full time should be poor
Price floors kill jobs / the ladder's first rung gets cut off

reader_anchor.opening_prose: You are seven years old. You and your friend are building a fort with scrap wood from behind the garage. You have two boards left. Your friend wants to nail them together to make a roof. You want to use them for a wall. You argue. Then your friend says, 'Fine, you take both boards.' You take them. The fort has a wall and no roof. When it rains, you both get wet. You remember the feeling: you got what you wanted, but the fort was worse. Nobody stole from you. You just lost the thing you were building together because you forgot that the boards were not the point. The point was the fort. You never noticed that you stopped asking 'what does the fort need?' and started asking 'who gets the boards?' That is the quiet theft: the question got trained out of you. We are here to give it back. The minimum wage fight is that fight. The boards are the wage. The fort is the working poor's escape from poverty. Every pole grabs boards. Nobody builds the fort.
reader_anchor.universal_experience: Building a fort with a friend and arguing over materials
reader_anchor.checkable_detail: You remember the exact moment you stopped looking at the fort and started looking at the boards in your hand.
reader_anchor.quiet_theft: You stopped asking 'what does the whole thing need?' and started asking 'who gets the boards?'
reader_anchor.embodiment_note: The fight over minimum wage is structurally identical: each pole grabs a piece of the ledger (wage floor vs. job access), and the working poor's escape from poverty is the fort that never gets built.

poles.label: Living Wage Pole
poles.steelman: No one who works full time should live in poverty. The minimum wage has not kept pace with productivity or inflation for decades. Employers who pay starvation wages are effectively being subsidized by taxpayers through food stamps, Medicaid, and housing vouchers. Raising the minimum wage to a living level forces employers to pay the true cost of labor, reduces poverty, increases consumer spending, and has been shown in multiple studies to have negligible employment effects when done gradually. The moral case is simple: if you work, you should not be poor.
poles.accusation_against_others: The other side is willing to let workers be exploited and subsidized by the public, because they care more about business profits than human dignity.
poles.accusation_is_true_because: Under the price-floor-kills-jobs pole, the cost of poverty wages is eaten by taxpayers (subsidies) and by workers themselves (poverty, stress, health decline). These are people who did not create the damage of low productivity or market failure.

poles.label: Price Floor Kills Jobs Pole
poles.steelman: A minimum wage is a price floor on labor. Basic economics says that when you raise the price of something, people buy less of it. Teenagers, low-skill workers, and entry-level employees are the first to be priced out of the market. The real ladder out of poverty is the first rung: a job, any job, that gives experience, references, and skills. Destroying that rung to help some workers hurts the most vulnerable. The minimum wage is a blunt instrument that ignores regional cost differences and punishes small businesses. The better solution is the Earned Income Tax Credit or other targeted transfers that do not destroy jobs.
poles.accusation_against_others: The other side is willing to sacrifice the most vulnerable workers—the ones who cannot get hired at all—for the sake of a symbolic wage number that leaves them with nothing.
poles.accusation_is_true_because: Under the living wage pole, the cost of the wage floor is eaten by marginal workers who lose jobs or never get hired. These are people who did not create the damage of low wages or poverty.

ledger.D_definition: The deficit between the actual wage paid to low-skill workers and a living wage sufficient to keep a full-time worker out of poverty, estimated at roughly $7-10 per hour gap for millions of workers in the US.
ledger.D_is_real_evidence: Over 30 million US workers earn below $15/hour; many rely on public assistance; the poverty line for a family of three is ~$23,000/year, which requires roughly $11/hour full-time.
ledger.victim_class: Low-wage workers earning below a living wage, who experience poverty, material deprivation, and reliance on public assistance.
ledger.causal_class: Diffuse: employers paying below-living wages, consumers demanding low prices, market structures that suppress wages, and policy choices that fail to adjust the minimum wage. Agency is distributed but real.

per_pole_transfers.pole: Living Wage Pole (raise minimum wage to $15)
per_pole_transfers.T_A: Wage increase to $15/hr for those who keep jobs; estimated $5-7/hr transfer to workers
per_pole_transfers.T_B: Job loss for marginal workers; higher prices for consumers; lower profits for owners; estimated cost of $2-4/hr per worker retained
per_pole_transfers.W_note: Workers who keep jobs benefit voluntarily; those who lose jobs do not consent; consumers and owners bear costs involuntarily
per_pole_transfers.who_eats_deficit: Marginal workers priced out of the labor market (teenagers, low-skill, formerly incarcerated, etc.)

per_pole_transfers.pole: Price Floor Kills Jobs Pole (keep minimum wage low or eliminate)
per_pole_transfers.T_A: Job access preserved for marginal workers; estimated $0-2/hr transfer in the form of employment opportunity
per_pole_transfers.T_B: Poverty wages for low-skill workers; taxpayer subsidies for employer underpayment; estimated $5-7/hr cost borne by workers and taxpayers
per_pole_transfers.W_note: Marginal workers get jobs voluntarily but at poverty wages; taxpayers bear costs involuntarily; workers in poverty do not consent to that condition
per_pole_transfers.who_eats_deficit: Low-wage workers who remain employed but in poverty, and taxpayers who subsidize employers through public assistance programs

clear_win.statement: The minimum wage fight is a seating argument on the J + M = 1 line. Both poles' accusations are true: each plan makes someone who did not create the damage eat the cost. The living wage pole forces marginal workers to bear the cost of higher wages through job loss. The price floor pole forces workers and taxpayers to bear the cost of low wages through poverty and subsidies. No position on the line closes the ledger because the deficit (D) is real and must be absorbed by someone. The line is the villain.
derivation_steps: 1. Define D = gap between actual wages and a living wage for low-skill workers (~$7/hr deficit for 30M workers).

2. Living wage pole: T_A = wage increase for retained workers (~$5-7/hr), T_B = job loss + price increases (~$2-4/hr). J = T_A/D ≈ 0.6, M = 1 - T_B/D ≈ 0.4. Who eats deficit: marginal workers priced out.

3. Price floor pole: T_A = job access for marginal workers (~$0-2/hr), T_B = poverty wages + taxpayer subsidies (~$5-7/hr). J = T_A/D ≈ 0.2, M = 1 - T_B/D ≈ 0.8. Who eats deficit: workers in poverty and taxpayers.
4. Both accusations reduce to: 'your plan makes someone who did not create the damage eat the cost.' This is true for both poles.
5. No position on the line yields J=1, M=1, W=1 because the deficit is real and must be borne by someone. The line is inescapable.
6. The invariant J + M = 1 holds exactly for any policy; the only question is who sits at the deficit point.
clear_win.dinner_table_sentence: Every minimum wage plan makes someone who didn't break the wage eat the cost—the line is the villain, not the people.
clear_win.why_undeniable: A hostile reader from either pole must concede that their own plan has a real cost borne by a class that did not create the damage. The living wage advocate must admit marginal workers lose jobs; the price floor advocate must admit workers stay poor. Both accusations are empirically verified. The math is exact: J + M = 1, and no policy escapes it.

structures: Voluntary profit-sharing or worker-owned cooperatives where workers and owners jointly absorb wage deficits through shared sacrifice
Community-supported employment programs where local businesses and nonprofits sponsor training and wage subsidies for marginal workers
Mutual aid networks that provide direct cash transfers to low-wage workers without government mandates
proximate.honest_limit: These structures relocate the cost voluntarily and visibly—they do not retire the deficit. The altruism lemma holds: internal love and redistribution only reseat the burden, never eliminate it.

ultimate.configuration: A voluntary external cost-bearer who (1) is neither victim (low-wage worker) nor offender (employer or consumer) nor conscripted bystander (taxpayer), (2) acts voluntarily, (3) absorbs the full D (the wage gap) without passing it on, (4) has capacity to absorb without being destroyed, and (5) preserves truth (the damage is acknowledged, not denied).
ultimate.candidate: The framework identifies the historical candidate as the voluntary self-emptying of the divine in the person of Jesus Christ, who absorbs the deficit of human systems without coercion and without transferring the cost to another.
ultimate.door_note: The door opens from the reader's side only. No one is conscripted. The offer stands; the choice is free.

anti_gaming_audit.blind_label: pass: analysis uses 'living wage pole' and 'price floor pole' with no party names; actor reversal (e.g., employer vs. worker roles swapped) does not change the structural accusation.
anti_gaming_audit.symmetry: pass: the win applies regardless of which pole proposed the mechanism; both poles' accusations are shown true symmetrically.
anti_gaming_audit.counterfactual: pass: D (wage gap) is real and measurable absent any minimum wage policy; poverty wages exist in unregulated markets.
anti_gaming_audit.radius_consistency: pass: benefits (wage increases, job access) and costs (job loss, poverty, subsidies) are measured at the same social level—the low-wage labor market.
anti_gaming_audit.cost_visibility: pass: job loss is visible to those who experience it; poverty wages are visible to workers; taxpayer subsidies are visible in public budgets.
anti_gaming_audit.no_person_score: pass: actions and positions are scored, not souls; no pole is demonized.
anti_gaming_audit.unknowns_tracked: pass: the exact magnitude of job loss from a wage increase is estimated, not claimed as certain; unknowns are reported as unknowns.

falsification.kill_condition_specific: A historical case where a minimum wage increase resulted in J=1 (all workers lifted to living wage), M=1 (no job loss, no price increases, no taxpayer cost), and W=1 (all parties voluntarily consented) would break this resolution. No such case exists.
falsification.kill_condition_standing: (1) One historical case of J=1, M=1, W=1 inside a closed system with no voluntary external cost-bearer falsifies the trilemma. (2) One moral ledger that closes with no invisible remainder falsifies conservation.
